item.title: Zuiryuji Temple: A National Treasure Zen Complex in Takaoka — Guide
item.description: Zuiryuji Temple was built in the mid-17th century by Maeda Toshitsune, second lord of the powerful Kaga domain, to honour his father and predecessor, and today stands as one of the finest surviving examples of early Edo-period Zen temple architecture in Japan. Its main hall, sanmon gate and dharma hall are all designated National Treasures, connected by covered corridors in a symmetrical layout characteristic of formal Zen temple design, offering visitors a rare chance to walk through a complete, historically intact temple complex.
